description: Make manual Agent launch idempotent and durably observable: one client call identity creates one Job, Session, initial Input, and initial Turn; reconnecting clients observe their authoritative state without replaying work.

tasks.title: Durable idempotent manual Agent launch
tasks.spec: specs/agent-launch-idempotency/spec.md#A call identity has one launch outcome
tasks.description: Replace the manual random-ID open-then-submit path with the `Idempotency-Key`-keyed `AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain`. The coordinator must persist the canonical launch plan and one-at-a-time command fence, prepare the AgentJob, atomically create the AgentSession's first accepted Input and queued Turn, then submit the prepared Job; update the Runner contract so it carries those identities and does not create a second initial session.input event.
acceptanceCriteria: POST agent launch rejects a missing or empty Idempotency-Key. For an identity with no plan, it preserves the existing invalid prompt, unknown Agent/context, and archived Agent rejection gates and creates no plan.

For one (ProjectId, Idempotency-Key), concurrent and retried matching requests return the same Job, Session, Input, and Turn IDs and issue exactly one Job dispatch; different keys create independent launches.

The route looks up an existing plan before mutable Agent/context/runtime validation. A matching replay returns or resumes the original snapshot after Agent archive/rename or referenced-context mutation, while a replay whose normalized client request differs returns launch_idempotency_conflict and leaves the original plan and resources unchanged.

The coordinator resumes the same prepared command after activation, Server restart, or a failed participant acknowledgement; it never uses a cross-aggregate transaction or stores Job/Session business state as a second authority.

Before a launch returns accepted, its AgentSession durably contains one accepted initial Input and one queued initial Turn associated with the Job; Server restart or queueing preserves those identities and the input content.
AgentJob dispatch and Runner reports propagate the generated Input/Turn identities, and the Runner no longer publishes a duplicate initial session.input record for an AgentJob launch.

Server spec tests cover new-identity validation without plan creation, duplicate and concurrent retries, conflicting reuse, replay after Agent archive/rename and referenced-context mutation, all coordinator recovery fences, initial Input/Turn persistence, queue delay, and exactly-one dispatch using fake time, storage, and dispatch observers.

Runner tests cover identity propagation and no duplicate initial input using a fake Runtime and Server connection; npm test, npm run typecheck -w packages/runner, and npm test -w packages/runner pass.
tasks.output: Idempotency-Key launch boundary; AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain and participant commands; durable initial SessionInput/AgentTurn records; AgentJob dispatch and Runner correlation update.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1-D3. The coordinator is a narrow durable application process manager: it persists only canonical command payload and delivery fence, invokes one participant aggregate per command, and resumes through durable retry. Scope is manual Web/CLI launch only; routed, mention, and follow-up paths remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Unknown-safe launch reconciliation and observation API
tasks.description: Make an inconclusive initial execution observable as Unknown instead of Failed or replayable, and reconcile it only against the original Job/work/Input/Turn identity after Runner reconnect. Add the project-scoped composite launch observation read API and expanded launch response so callers can retrieve authoritative Job, Session, Input, Turn, and transcript references without turning Input or Turn into top-level resources.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentJob and the initial AgentTurn expose Unknown as a nonterminal, non-dispatchable state; Runner loss or inconclusive delivery never fabricates failed, idle, completed, or a second prompt submission.
Runner reconnect reconciliation uses the original Job/work identity: authoritative running and terminal reports update the original Turn and Job, while inconclusive evidence leaves them Unknown.

GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-jobs/{jobId}/launch-observation enforces project isolation and returns a composite DTO with authoritative Job status/result, Session activity/runtime/transcript reference, initial Input acceptance, and initial Turn status/result.

The launch 201 response returns Job, Session, Input, and Turn IDs plus the observation URL; existing focused Job, Session, and transcript reads remain valid and reads create no new Input, Turn, or Job.
A completed initial Job leaves its AgentSession usable; queued Input/Turn state does not claim the Job completed or failed before an authoritative result.

Server and Runner tests cover Unknown on Runner disconnect, reconciliation to running or terminal, no replay, composite observation during queued/running/terminal/Unknown states, repeated observation, and cross-project rejection with fakes only.
npm test, npm run typecheck -w packages/runner, and npm test -w packages/runner pass.
tasks.output: Unknown Job/Turn convergence contract; original-work Runner reconciliation; AgentLaunchObservationDto and project-scoped launch-observation route; expanded launch response.
tasks.notes: Implements design D4-D5. It consumes T-001's stable initial Input/Turn IDs and coordinator-linked Job/Session. The observation assembler is read-only: Job remains the result authority and Session remains the authority for activity, children, and transcript.

tasks.title: Web and CLI resilient launch experience
tasks.spec: specs/agent-launch-observation/spec.md#Web and CLI use the same launch-state meaning and recovery guidance
tasks.description: Adopt the idempotent launch and composite observation contract in the Web composer/session view and `mo agent launch`. Web retains a generated key for a pending launch retry; CLI forwards an explicit or generated key, prints it before dispatch when generated, returns all four identities and the observation location, and both clients render the same server-defined pending, executing, terminal, and Unknown meanings without inferring Job results from Session activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Web generates one Idempotency-Key before its first launch mutation, preserves it for retry after response loss, and navigates only to the Session returned by that launch rather than creating a replacement attempt.

mo agent launch accepts --idempotency-key, forwards it unchanged, and when it generates one, prints it before the request so a later invocation can retry with that value; in-process retries reuse the same key.
Successful Web and CLI launches expose the stable Job, Session, Input, and Turn identities and the composite observation location.

Web and CLI consume the composite observation DTO for status meaning: pending/queued/executing direct the user to observe, terminal states direct to result/transcript, and Unknown directs a re-read or retry with the original key rather than a new launch.
The Session view continues to show transcript updates after reconnect and does not mark the Session closed when the initial Job is terminal.

Web tests cover retained-key mutation retry, returned-identity navigation, DTO-driven queued/terminal/Unknown rendering, and no client-side Job-from-Session inference; CLI tests cover key forwarding/reuse guidance, four-id output, and observation output.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web, npm run test:run -w packages/web, npm run check:fsd -w packages/web, and npm test pass.
tasks.output: Web idempotent launch mutation and observation-driven Session UI; CLI idempotency-key option/output and four-reference launch presentation; aligned client recovery guidance.
tasks.notes: Implements the client portions of design D1 and D5. This task adds no follow-up, cancellation, Slack, or separate Input/Turn management surface. Update the relevant Agent and CLI product documentation when the user-visible command and recovery contract lands.
